claim: Which thiolactone block lipidoid L6 is built from.
locus_a: SI p.17 Table S2 row L6: 'T18u-PY18-A4' (lower-case u)
locus_b: SI pp.2-6 and every other Table S2 row: 'T18U' (upper-case U), and the library has exactly four thiolactones
why: A case slip in one table cell. 'T18u' names no block anywhere in the SI; the library is 4x4x18 and T18U is the fourth thiolactone. Normalised in stage05_values.py's CASE_SLIPS, with the printed form kept in the column structure_name_as_printed so the slip is not erased.

claim: The chain length of pyridyl disulfide PY12.
locus_a: SI p.5: 'Synthesis of Pyridyl Disulfide Derivative, 2-(DECYLdisulfanyl) pyridine (P12)' -- decyl is C10
locus_b: Its own printed HRMS on SI p.6, C17H29NS2 at m/z 312.1821, which is 2-(DODECYLdisulfanyl)pyridine; and Scheme S1b (SI p.2) draws that reagent with 12 stroked bonds from the HS label (stage01_chains.py, vector)
why: Two independent lines -- mass and drawn geometry -- agree against the name. A decyl compound would be C15H25NS2, [M+H]+ 284.151, 28 Da away from the printed value, and the drawn chain would have 10 bonds, not 12. The label 'PY12' also agrees with C12. This is the AC_2025 situation in reverse: there the NAMES were wrong and the structures right; here the name is wrong and the formula, the mass, the drawing and the label are all right. Queued as D-8 because one emittable row (L11, T16-PY12-A1) depends on it.

claim: The molecular formula of thiolactone T18U.
locus_a: SI p.3: 'HRMS (ESI): m/z calcd for C29H40NO2S [M+H]+ : 382.2782' (verified by rendering the line at 600 dpi, not only by text extraction)
locus_b: The same line's m/z. 382.2782 requires C22H40NO2S+; C29H40NO2S+ is 466.27. The drawn structure in Scheme S1a is oleamide + homocysteine thiolactone = C22H39NO2S.
why: A typographical error in the carbon subscript. The mass, the drawing and the series (T14 C18, T16 C20, T18 C22) all agree on C22; only the subscript does not. Our structure is 0.77 mDa from the authors' own printed m/z (03_block_hrms.json).

claim: Whether the printed HRMS formulae are the neutral molecule or the [M+H]+ ion.
locus_a: SI p.4 P18 'C23H42NS2 [M+H]+' and p.3 T18 'C22H42NO2S [M+H]+' -- both PROTONATED formulae
locus_b: SI p.6 P12 'C17H29NS2 [M+H]+' and p.4 T14 'C18H33NO2S [M+H]+' -- both NEUTRAL formulae, one hydrogen short of the ion they are labelled as
what_we_emitted: structures, from the masses and the drawings; no formula is taken from the printed subscripts
why: The convention is inconsistent within the same SI. It changes no structure -- every printed m/z is reproduced by the neutral molecule plus one proton -- but it is why stage01_chains.py uses only the CARBON subscript of these formulae and never the hydrogen count.

claim: How many distinct lipidoids Table S2 lists.
locus_a: SI p.17 Table S2: 45 rows, L1 to L45; Figure S3's caption says '45 lipidoids which have transfection efficiency >= 40%'
locus_b: The same table: L17 and L18 are both 'T16-PY18-A13' at 57, and L26 is 'T16-PY18-A13' at 50. 45 rows carry only 43 distinct structure names.
what_we_emitted: all 45 rows as printed, with the repeat recorded in 05_values_summary.json; none of the three is emittable (A13 is undetermined)
why: Either two rows are duplicates of one measurement or one or two names are mistyped, and the SI gives no way to tell which. Not repaired: repairing a name is how 419 measurements were nearly put on the wrong molecules in AC_2025. DECISIONS.md D-7.

claim: The rank order of the 45 lipidoids.
locus_a: SI p.17 Table S2, printed %TE, strictly non-increasing L1 -> L45
locus_b: SI p.17 Figure S3, the same 45 lipidoids drawn as bars. Under a calibration taken only from the y-axis ticks, L22 (printed 52) is drawn ABOVE L21 (printed 55), and L29 (printed 50) above four lipidoids printed at 52-55.
what_we_emitted: the printed %TE from Table S2; the figure is used only to verify (04_figS3_verification.json)
why: The two panels of one experiment disagree on rank in two places out of 42 readable bars. Everything else matches: drawn/printed ratio CV 2.30%, Pearson 0.9965, and the figure's own positive-control bar lands 0.64% from the 1.000 it must be. The printed numerals are the higher-tier source, so they are what is stored; the disagreement is recorded rather than averaged away.

claim: Which amine Figure S1 panel b) plots.
locus_a: SI p.15 caption: 'Plot of absorbance vs time for b) A1 and d) A10'
locus_b: Panel b) itself carries an inset structure labelled A5, and panel a) -- the spectra the b) trace is taken from -- is described in the same caption as 'primary amine A5' with every legend entry reading 'after adding A5'
what_we_emitted: A5, and A5's structure is measured from that panel's inset (01_amines.json)
why: The caption's 'A1' is a slip: the panel, its own inset label, and the companion panel all say A5. This matters because panel b) is one of only two places in the SI where an amine other than A1 is drawn at all.

claim: The name of the pyridyl disulfide blocks.
locus_b: SI p.2 Scheme S1, SI p.7 Scheme S2 and every lipidoid name in Table S2: 'PY18', 'PY16', 'PY14', 'PY12'
what_we_emitted: PY18 / PY16 / PY14 / PY12, the form the lipidoid names use
why: Two label sets for the same four compounds. Harmless on its own, recorded because keying on the wrong one would silently drop every HRMS cross-check.

claim: How many lipidoids have transfection efficiency above 60%.
locus_a: SI p.21, Figure S9 and Figure S10 captions: 'Cell viability of top 11 lipidoids which have transfection efficiency more than 60%'
locus_b: SI p.17 Table S2: twelve lipidoids are printed above 60 (L1-L12, 95 down to 65) and two more are at exactly 60 (L13, L14). The eleven named in the Figure S9 legend are exactly L1-L11, which stops one short of its own stated criterion.
what_we_emitted: nothing -- Figures S9/S10 are viability, not a delivery endpoint, and were not digitised
why: Recorded because the ELEVEN NAMES THEMSELVES are a load-bearing cross-check: they are text objects, so pdfplumber recovers them at tier 4 and they match Table S2's raster rows L1-L11 exactly and in order (07_qc.json CROSS_TIER). The caption's threshold is loose; the membership is not, and it is the membership the check uses.
